ch41.note: Lin Biao's Manchurian army passed through a run of names—the Northeast People's Liberation Army, then the Northeast Field Army, and in 1949 the Fourth Field Army, one of the four great field armies of the People's Liberation Army—which then swept south through the country. The names all mean the same force.

'Reorganization' (改编) is the Communist term for breaking up a surrendered Nationalist unit and folding its men into the People's Liberation Army; Chen notes bitterly that Fu Zuoyi's reorganized troops were then thrown straight into the front line against Taiyuan.

Deng Baoshan (邓宝珊, 1894–1968), a general of the old Northwest Army holding a deputy commander-in-chief's rank under Fu Zuoyi, was the intermediary who negotiated Fu's peaceful handover of Beiping to the Communists in January 1949.

The 'Yuan big-head' (袁大头) was the silver dollar stamped with the profile of Yuan Shikai, first president of the Republic, minted from 1914. Its honest silver content made it the coin people trusted when paper money failed—here the hard currency against which the collapsing gold-yuan note is measured.

ch41.anchor: food and sex are of nature
ch41.note: A maxim from the Mencius, spoken by the philosopher Gaozi: 'the appetite for food and the appetite for sex are of our nature' (食色，性也)—the bodily desires are inborn, not learned. Chen uses it wryly as a section heading.
